citations.claim: First violation: body 0 grazes top-left corner of wall 0 with 0.1565 overlap exceeding 0.15 limit
One step before, body already penetrating corner by 0.032 showing progressive sink while sliding past corner
Two steps before, body 0.09 from surface, approaching corner with high downward speed
Earlier approach 0.21 from surface showing monotonic closing onto corner

counterfactual.change: Set vx from 1.34 to 0 so body falls vertically and misses the wall corner entirely; same 34 steps, no violation, proving corner-graze geometry causes the sink.

explanation: Body falls diagonally (vx~1.34, vy~-7.3) past the top-left corner (9.1,5.0) of thin wall. Corner distance shrinks monotonically (+0.21 at 31, +0.09 at 32, -0.032 at 33, -0.156 at 34) while velocity stays downward, so impulse plus positional correction fails to push the circle out of the rounded-corner contact and penetration accumulates past the 0.15 tolerance. Removing horizontal motion avoids the corner and removes the failure.
vision_note: The red circle falls down onto the top end of the thin vertical grey wall. It makes contact and then sinks progressively deeper into the top of the wall from step 32 to step 34 instead of bouncing or resting on it.
